subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Sensorimotor Stage
description: A fast breakdown of The Sensorimotor Stage for builders.

hook.text: Hide a toy under a blanket and a six-month-old stops looking. Out of sight, out of mind—literally.

buildup.text: Piaget's first stage (birth to two) says babies think by doing—grabbing, sucking, shaking.

discovery.text: Around eight months, object permanence appears. The baby searches for hidden objects at last.

twist.text: But the A-not-B error lingers: hide a toy at B after hiding at A, and the baby checks A again.

climax.text: By age two, toddlers can mentally represent absent objects. Thought is no longer tied to action.

punchline.text: First you act, then you imagine acting.

quiz.question: What milestone emerges in the sensorimotor stage?
